name: Switzerland
tagline: Cheap tuition, brutal living costs, and a very specific IB rule
summary: Switzerland publishes one of the clearest IB rules in Europe and one of the strictest. swissuniversities sets a minimum of 32 out of 42 points and a fixed six-subject structure; ETH Zurich and EPFL raise the bar to 38 points and dictate exactly which subjects must sit at Higher Level. Tuition is low by international standards, but Switzerland is not outside the EU by accident - it is expensive to live in, and almost every bachelor's degree is taught in German, French or Italian. English-taught bachelor's exist, but they are mostly at small private institutions.
whyConsider: ETH Zurich and EPFL are among the strongest science and engineering universities in the world, and tuition is a fraction of what an equivalent place costs in the UK or the US.
The rules are written down. swissuniversities publishes exactly which IB subjects and how many points are needed, so you can check your eligibility in Y1 rather than guess.
As an EU/EFTA citizen you get a straightforward student residence permit and access to part-time work.
Small countries, short distances, and universities with genuinely close contact between staff and students - USI quotes one lecturer per seven students.
If you already have strong German, French or Italian, the whole public system opens up to you at very low tuition.
watchOuts: ETH doubled down on international students: from autumn semester 2025 the tuition for foreign students is CHF 2,190 per semester against CHF 730 for Swiss residents. Coming straight from Denmark, you pay the higher rate.

ETH requires Maths, a natural science and a Language A all at Higher Level. An IB student with HL Maths, HL Physics and three SLs including Visual Arts or Psychology falls outside the rule and faces an entrance examination in German.
The ETH entrance examination route runs on a very long lead time - for autumn 2027 entry the application deadline was 31 March 2026 and the exam was held 18-28 January 2027.
Language, not grades, is what stops most Danish IB students: ETH teaches bachelor's in German, the University of Zurich requires German at C1, and EPFL requires French at B2.
Living costs are the highest in Europe. Budget accordingly - this research could not verify current official figures, so get them from your target university before committing.
EPFL has capped its first-year bachelor intake at 3,000 students from 2025, with Swiss maturity holders guaranteed admission and everyone else ranked.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: 32 out of 42 points (bonus points not counted) at most Swiss universities. ETH Zurich and EPFL require 38 out of 42.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: swissuniversities requires six subjects, one from each of six categories: (1) first language; (2) second language (any recognised language); (3) mathematics, HL or SL; (4) natural sciences - biology, chemistry, physics or computer science; (5) humanities and social sciences - geography, history, economics, business management or philosophy; (6) an elective from categories 2, 4 or 5, or computer science or philosophy. Computer science and philosophy may only be used as the sixth subject. At least three of the six must be Higher Level, and one of those Higher Level subjects must be mathematics or another natural science. ETH Zurich is stricter still: admission without an entrance examination requires 38/42 points; at Higher Level you must have (a) Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, (b) physics, chemistry or biology, and (c) one Language A; at Standard Level you must have three further subjects from physics, chemistry, biology, geography, history, economics or business management, one further language only, or computer science. EPFL requires Mathematics, Physics and one of chemistry, biology or computer science at Higher Level; two modern languages and one of history, geography, economics or philosophy at SL or HL; 38/42 points; and grades of at least 6 out of 7 in mathematics and physics.
notes: The ETH rule is exclusive, not illustrative. Subjects that do not appear on its Standard Level list - for example Visual Arts, Theatre, Psychology, Global Politics or Environmental Systems and Societies - do not count towards the three required SL subjects, and the consequence is the ETH entrance examination, which is held in German.

The ETH entrance examination comes in two forms: reduced (CHF 550) and comprehensive (CHF 800), covering mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, history, geography and languages. ETH decides which one applies only after you have submitted a complete application.
EPFL applies lower thresholds to Swiss applicants (36 points and grade 5/7 in maths and physics) than to everyone else, so the 38-point bar is the one that applies to a Danish student.
The swissuniversities requirements were published as valid for 2026/27 and are updated annually - re-check them in autumn 2026 for the 2027/28 rules.
No official conversion of IB points into Swiss grades (1-6) was found published. Swiss admission is generally pass/fail against the threshold rather than ranked by a converted grade.

portal.name: Each university applies directly; swissuniversities publishes the shared admission recommendations

deadlines.label: ETH Zurich - application when an entrance examination will be needed (autumn 2027 entry)
deadlines.date: 31 March 2026 (application); exam registration 15 September to 15 October 2026; examination 18-28 January 2027
deadlines.notes: This is the published timetable for starting in autumn semester 2027. If your IB subject combination does not meet the exam-free rule, you had to be in the system eighteen months ahead. Do not discover this in your final year.

deadlines.label: ETH Zurich - ordinary bachelor application deadline for the autumn semester
deadlines.notes: Could not be verified from an official ETH page during this research. ETH states that it can only decide whether you need an entrance examination once a complete application has been submitted through eApply, so apply as early as the portal allows. Confirm the date and any application fee on ethz.ch.

deadlines.label: EPFL - admission decision timing for holders of an IB or EU/EFTA certificate
deadlines.date: Admissions confirmed at the beginning of August, within the places available
deadlines.notes: EPFL ranks eligible applicants by overall academic performance because first-year places are capped at 3,000 from 2025. The application deadline itself was not verified from an official page in this research.

deadlines.label: Other Swiss universities (Zurich, Bern, Basel, Geneva, Lausanne, Fribourg, Lucerne, Neuchatel, St Gallen, USI)
deadlines.notes: Deadlines are set by each university and are typically in late winter or spring for the following autumn - much earlier than in Germany or Austria. This research could not verify the individual dates; take them from each university's admission page in autumn 2026.

steps: In Y1, before your subject choices are locked, check your six subjects against the swissuniversities rule and, if you are aiming at ETH or EPFL, against their stricter rules.
Decide on the teaching language early. German at C1 or French at B2 is a year or more of work, and it is the requirement most Danish IB students underestimate.
By autumn 2026, take the application deadline from each university's own page - Swiss deadlines fall much earlier than German or Austrian ones.
If ETH is the target and your combination does not meet the exam-free rule, apply in time for the entrance examination cycle, which starts more than a year ahead.
Submit the application with predicted grades and school documents, and send the final Diploma as soon as it arrives in early July 2027.
Once admitted, arrange the residence permit, compulsory Swiss health insurance and housing - all three take time and all three cost more than you expect.
application.selectionNotes: Most Swiss universities admit on qualification rather than ranking: meet the points, the subject rule and the language requirement and you are in. The exceptions matter, though. Medicine is restricted nationally and uses an aptitude test. EPFL now caps first-year bachelor places and ranks non-Swiss applicants by academic performance. ETH funnels anyone outside its exact IB rule into a German-language entrance examination. The University of St Gallen operates a cap on the share of students with foreign school-leaving certificates; the exact figure could not be verified in this research.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Rare. Swiss public universities teach bachelor's in German, French or Italian - ETH's bachelor programmes are in German, the University of Zurich requires German at C1 from foreign applicants, and EPFL requires French at B2 with C1 recommended. English-taught bachelor's are mostly found at private and specialist institutions such as Franklin University Switzerland, Webster Geneva and EHL. English comes into its own at master's level, where much of the Swiss system switches over.
language.englishProof: Not a barrier on its own - IB English A is accepted where English proficiency is required. The binding requirement is usually the local teaching language, not English.
notes: ETH: "The main teaching language in all Bachelor's degree programmes is German."
University of Zurich requires German at C1 on the Common European Framework from applicants with foreign certificates.
EPFL requires French at level B2 for its bachelor's, and strongly recommends C1.
USI's Communication bachelor requires Italian at B2 for non-native speakers.
If you are not already strong in one of these languages, Switzerland is realistically a master's destination rather than a bachelor's one - unless you pay for a private English-taught school.

tuitionEuEea.value: There is no EU/non-EU split in Switzerland - the split is between students with Swiss residence or citizenship and everyone else. A Danish student moving from Denmark counts as a foreign student. At ETH Zurich that means CHF 2,190 per semester rather than CHF 730.

tuitionNonEu.value: ETH Zurich charges CHF 2,190 per semester (threefold tuition) to foreign students who were not resident in Switzerland or Liechtenstein when they obtained their entrance qualification; CHF 730 per semester applies to Swiss and Liechtenstein citizens and residents, and to certain EU/EFTA citizens with qualifying permits. Students already enrolled before autumn 2025 keep the old rate until they finish. Fees at other Swiss universities were not verified in this research.

notes: The ETH entrance examination costs CHF 550 (reduced) or CHF 800 (comprehensive), on top of any application fee.

Living costs are by a wide margin the biggest number in a Swiss budget and this research could not verify an official figure from a university page. ETH publishes a 'Costs of living' document via ethz.ch/students/en/studies/financial.html - get the current figure from there, and from your target university, before you commit.
Compulsory Swiss basic health insurance is an extra monthly cost on top of rent and food. The premium and the exemption rules for EU students could not be verified here.
Application fees at Swiss universities are usually charged per application and are non-refundable, but no amount could be verified from an official page in this research.

funding: Danish SU can in many cases be taken abroad for a full degree - check with SU Styrelsen, because Swiss living costs make this the decisive factor.
The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are aimed at postgraduate and research level, not at bachelor's entry - do not build a plan around them.
Individual universities run their own hardship and merit funds; ETH's Financial Aid Office is the contact point there.
Private English-taught institutions such as Franklin and EHL run their own scholarship schemes, which can change the real price significantly - ask for the net figure.
Erasmus+ works differently in Switzerland, which runs its own mobility programme rather than participating fully in Erasmus+.
workRights: EU/EFTA students in Switzerland may take part-time work alongside their studies, and the usual limit quoted is around 15 hours a week during term with full-time work permitted in holidays. This research could not confirm the rule from an official page, so check with your university's international office or the cantonal migration office before counting on the income.
residency: Switzerland is not in the EU, but EU/EFTA citizens are covered by the free movement agreement and get a residence permit (permit B for students) rather than a visa. You register at the local commune within the period they specify after arriving, showing your admission letter, proof of financial means and health insurance. Non-EU students need a student visa arranged through a Swiss embassy well in advance.
housing: Zurich, Geneva and Lausanne have some of the tightest and most expensive rental markets in Europe, and student halls do not come close to covering demand. Start as soon as you have an offer, use the university's own housing service, and expect a shared flat rather than a studio. Lugano, St Gallen, Fribourg and Bern are noticeably easier.
healthcare: Swiss basic health insurance is compulsory for everyone living in Switzerland and you must take it out within three months of arriving unless you are granted an exemption. EU students may in some circumstances be exempted on the basis of European coverage, but the exemption is granted by the cantonal authority and is not automatic. Sort this out in your first weeks - the rules and the premium could not be verified from an official page here, so ask your university's international office directly.

institutions.name: ETH Zurich
institutions.englishBachelors: None - all bachelor's programmes are taught in German. English dominates at master's level.
institutions.note: The single most demanding IB rule in this country file: 38 points, and HL maths, HL science and HL Language A - otherwise you sit a German-language entrance exam.

institutions.name: EPFL - Ecole polytechnique federale de Lausanne
institutions.englishBachelors: None - the bachelor's is taught in French and requires French at B2.
institutions.note: Requires HL Maths, HL Physics and HL chemistry, biology or computer science, 38 points, and at least 6/7 in maths and physics - plus French.

institutions.name: University of Zurich
institutions.note: Switzerland's largest university; applies the swissuniversities IB rule and requires German at C1 from applicants with foreign certificates.

institutions.name: University of Geneva
institutions.note: French-speaking, next door to the UN and CERN; an obvious pick if international affairs is the plan and your French is real.

institutions.name: University of Basel
institutions.note: Switzerland's oldest university, German-speaking, at the heart of the Basel pharmaceutical cluster.

institutions.name: University of Bern
institutions.note: Strong climate and space research in the federal capital; German-speaking and less crowded than Zurich.

institutions.name: University of Lausanne
institutions.note: Shares a lakeside campus with EPFL, so you get a science campus and a broad general university next to each other; teaching is in French.

institutions.name: University of St. Gallen
institutions.note: The German-speaking world's best-known business school, with a famously strong recruiting network; it limits the share of students holding foreign school-leaving certificates, so verify the quota and the deadline directly.

institutions.name: Universita della Svizzera italiana
institutions.englishBachelors: Some - USI runs nine bachelor's including architecture, communication, economics, informatics and data science; check the language of each, as Communication requires Italian at B2.
institutions.note: Small Italian-speaking university on Lake Lugano with roughly one lecturer per seven students; the most approachable Swiss public university for an international student, but check the teaching language programme by programme.

institutions.name: University of Fribourg
institutions.note: Switzerland's bilingual university - you can study partly in German and partly in French, which is unusual and useful if you want to build both.

institutions.name: Franklin University Switzerland
institutions.englishBachelors: All bachelor's are taught in English, in a small American-style liberal arts structure.
institutions.note: Tiny English-language liberal arts college above Lake Lugano, accredited in both Switzerland and the US; tuition is in a different league from the public universities and could not be verified here.

institutions.name: EHL Hospitality Business School
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelor in International Hospitality Management, taught in English.
institutions.note: The world's best-known hospitality school, with paid internships built into the degree; private and fee-paying, and fees were not verified here.

institutions.name: University of Lucerne
institutions.note: Switzerland's smallest and newest public university, right by the lake and the mountains; German-speaking and strong in law and health policy.

institutions.name: Webster University Geneva
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught American bachelor's degrees, mainly in business, international relations, media and psychology.
institutions.note: The Geneva campus of an American university, teaching entirely in English; private, fee-paying, and fees were not verified here.
